transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I’ve been feeling wound up and on edge for months, like my mood is stuck on high and I’m snapping at everyone, even my own family. It's like I just can't slow down, and the smallest things make me lose my temper.
During these times when you feel 'stuck on high' and can't slow down, do you find that you need much less sleep than usual but still feel full of energy?

Yes, definitely. Most nights I only sleep about two or three hours because my mind is racing with so many ideas and plans, but I don't even feel tired. Instead of sleeping, I just get up and start cleaning, writing lists, or texting people in the middle of the night.
Have you ever experienced a period in your life lasting two weeks or more where you felt the exact opposite—very down, depressed, or completely lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Usually, I just crash and shut down for a few days at a time, skipping boxing and church because everything feels like too much effort. But a couple of months ago, I did have about two weeks where my mood felt completely flat, empty, and drained rather than amped up. Even during those weeks when I felt so low, the voices and the feeling that people were out to get me never let up.
Have you ever heard those voices or felt like people were out to get you during times when your mood was completely normal, without feeling high or low?

Yes, there was a time a couple of months ago when my mood wasn't super high or amped up, and I just felt flat and drained instead of manic. Even during those weeks when my mood was more leveled out, the voices and the feeling that people were watching and testing me didn't let up at all.

Have you ever had a period of two weeks or more where you heard those voices or felt people were watching you, but your mood felt completely normal—meaning you didn't feel high, manic, depressed, flat, or drained?

No, my mood wasn't completely normal during that time—it felt really flat and drained instead. But even though I wasn't feeling high or manic, the voices and that feeling of being watched never stopped.

Aside from that period when you felt flat and drained, has there ever been any other time in your life when you heard voices or felt watched for at least two weeks while your mood felt completely normal and balanced?

No, I don't think so. This whole thing has only been going on for about a year, and my mood has pretty much been either super high or crashed and flat. I've never had a time where I felt completely normal and balanced while still hearing those voices.
How long do these periods of being 'stuck on high' with racing thoughts and very little sleep typically last? Do they go on for a few days, a week, or even longer?

These periods of feeling wired and "stuck on high" actually last for months at a time. It has been going on continuously for about half a year now, with only very short, temporary crashes before I ramp right back up again.
During those two weeks when you felt flat and drained, did you also experience other symptoms like significant changes in your appetite, feelings of worthlessness, or thoughts of self-harm?

I don't recall having those specific feelings of worthlessness or thoughts of self-harm during that time. I just felt extremely shut down and lacked the energy to do basic things like showering or cooking, so I'd spend days just staring at the TV.
During those two weeks when you felt flat and drained, did you find yourself sleeping much more than usual, or did you have trouble concentrating?

I don't really remember if I was sleeping more or having trouble concentrating during those couple of weeks. I just remember feeling completely flat and drained, while still hearing those voices and feeling like people were watching me.

During that two-week period when you felt flat and drained, did you notice any significant changes in your weight or appetite, or did anyone comment that you were moving or speaking much slower than usual?

During that flat and drained period, I don't recall having any significant changes in my weight or appetite. I also don't remember anyone commenting that I was moving or speaking slower. I just felt completely shut down, exhausted, and barely talked to anyone.

opening_question.question: Hello, I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a current manic episode characterized by an irritable and elevated mood ('stuck on high'), a severely decreased need for sleep (sleeping only 2-3 hours per night while remaining energized), racing thoughts, and increased goal-directed activity (cleaning, writing lists, texting at night). These manic symptoms have been ongoing continuously for approximately six months. During this episode, the patient also experiences prominent psychotic symptoms, including auditory hallucinations ('hearing voices') and persecutory delusions ('feeling like people were out to get me, watching and testing me'). The patient denies any period of 2 weeks or more where psychotic symptoms occurred in the absence of prominent mood symptoms, ruling out schizoaffective disorder. Therefore, the presentation is most consistent with Bipolar Affective Disorder, Current Episode Manic with Psychotic Symptoms (ICD-10: F31.2).
